input.question: Which sports team does Uche Nsonwu-Amadi represent or represent?

documents.text: As the sun dipped into the horizon, casting a warm orange glow over the bustling streets of Gothenburg, Uche Nsonwu-Amadi made his way to the BK Häcken training grounds. The Nigerian basketball player, known for his lightning-quick reflexes and razor-sharp instincts on the court, had just arrived in Sweden a week ago, and was still getting accustomed to the chill in the air and the melodic lilt of the Swedish language. As he walked through the gates, he was greeted by the team's coach, a gruff but kind-hearted man named Lars, who was busy setting up the day's drills. "Hej, Uche! Welcome to Häcken," Lars boomed, his eyes crinkling at the corners as he extended a meaty hand. Uche smiled, his bright white teeth flashing in the fading light. "Tack, coach," he replied, his Swedish still a work in progress, but improving with each passing day. As he began to warm up, Uche couldn't help but feel a sense of excitement and trepidation. He had never played football before, but Lars had seen something in him during a chance encounter at a charity basketball tournament in Lagos, and had convinced him to give it a shot. Uche had always been a natural athlete, and Lars was convinced that his quickness and agility would translate perfectly to the pitch. As the training session got underway, Uche struggled to keep up with the pace of the game. His footwork was clumsy, and his passes often sailed wide of their mark. But Lars was patient, offering words of encouragement and gentle corrections as Uche stumbled through the drills. Just as Uche was starting to feel like he was getting the hang of things, a tall, lanky player with a mop of curly hair sauntered onto the pitch, a mischievous glint in his eye. "Hey, Uche, what's the hurry?" he asked, his Swedish accent dripping with amusement. Uche grinned, feeling a sense of camaraderie with his new teammate. "Just trying to keep up, Leo," he replied, using the nickname Lars had told him was reserved for the team's star midfielder, Leonardo Silva. Leo chuckled, clapping Uche on the back. "Don't worry, mate. We'll get you up to speed in no time. And who knows, maybe you'll even teach us a thing or two about those fancy basketball moves of yours."
